title.zh: 卷一百三十五 列傳第八十五: 盧杞 白志貞 裴延齡 韋渠牟 李齊運 李實 韋執誼 王叔文 程異 皇甫抃
title.en: Volume 135 Biographies 85: Lu Qi, Bai Zhizhen, Pei Yanling, Wei Qumou, Li Qiyun, Li Shi, Wei Zhiyi, Wang Shuwen, Cheng Yi, Huang Fubian
title.raw: 卷一百三十五 列傳第八十五: 盧杞 白志貞 裴延齡 韋渠牟 李齊運 李實 韋執誼 王叔文 程異 皇甫抃 Volume 135 Biographies 85: Lu Qi, Bai Zhizhen, Pei Yanling, Wei Qumou, Li Qiyun, Li Shi, Wei Zhiyi, Wang Shuwen, Cheng Yi, Huang Fubian

meta.sourceNote: Body replaced from Wikisource raw text after ChineseNotes scrape due to glyph/encoding artifacts.

sentences.zh: 陸贄陸贄，字敬輿，蘇州嘉興人。

translations.literal: Lu Zhi—Lu Zhi, courtesy name Jingyu, was a man of Jiaxing in Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi, whose courtesy name was Jingyu, was from Jiaxing in Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 父侃，溧陽令，以贄貴，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: His father Kan was magistrate of Liyang; because of Zhi's eminence he was posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: His father Lu Kan had served as magistrate of Liyang; when Zhi rose to prominence, Kan was posthumously honored as Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 贄少孤，特立不群，頗勤儒學。

translations.literal: Zhi was orphaned in youth, stood apart from others, and was quite diligent in Confucian studies.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned while young, he held himself apart from the crowd and applied himself diligently to classical learning.

sentences.zh: 年十八登進士第，以博學宏詞登科，授華州鄭縣尉。

translations.literal: At age eighteen he passed the jinshi examination; through the Broad Learning and Grand Rhetoric subject he obtained a degree and was appointed defender of Zheng County in Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen he earned his jinshi degree and also passed the Broad Learning and Grand Rhetoric examination, receiving appointment as magistrate of Zheng County in Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 罷秩，東歸省母，路由壽州，刺史張鎰有時名，贄往謁之。

translations.literal: When his term ended, he traveled east to visit his mother; his route passed through Shou Prefecture, where Prefect Zhang Yi enjoyed a certain reputation, and Zhi went to call on him.
translations.idiomatic: After leaving office he headed east to see his mother. Passing through Shou Prefecture, he paid a visit to the prefect Zhang Yi, who was then well regarded.

sentences.zh: 鎰初不甚知，留三日，再見與語，遂大稱賞，請結忘年之契。

translations.literal: Yi at first did not know him well; after three days' stay, on a second meeting and conversation, he greatly praised and esteemed him and asked to form a bond transcending their difference in age.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi scarcely noticed him at first, but after Zhi stayed three days and they met and spoke again, Yi was deeply impressed and proposed a friendship that ignored the gap in their ages.

sentences.zh: 及辭，遺贄錢百萬，曰：「願備太夫人一日之膳。

translations.literal: When he took leave, he left Zhi a gift of a million cash, saying, "I wish to supply the Senior Lady's meals for a day.
translations.idiomatic: As Zhi was departing, Zhang Yi offered him a million cash, saying, "Let this help provide your mother's board for a day.

sentences.zh: 」贄不納，唯受新茶一串而已，曰：「敢不承君厚意。

translations.literal: " Zhi did not accept it, taking only a single string of new tea, and said, "I dare not fail to acknowledge your generous kindness.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhi declined the money and accepted only one bundle of fresh tea, adding, "I shall not fail to honor your gracious intent.

sentences.zh: 」又以書判拔萃，選授渭南縣主簿，遷監察御史。

translations.literal: " He also passed the Outstanding Case Judgment selection and was appointed chief clerk of Weinan County, then promoted to investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: " He next distinguished himself in documentary review, was selected as chief clerk of Weinan County, and was later transferred to investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 德宗在東宮時，素知贄名，乃召為翰林學士，轉祠部員外郎。

translations.literal: When Dezong was Eastern Heir, he had long known Zhi's name and summoned him as Hanlin academician, then transferred him to Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: While still crown prince, Dezong had known Zhi's reputation and now summoned him as Hanlin academician, promoting him shortly afterward to Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 贄性忠盡，既居近密，感人主重知，思有以效報，故政或有缺，巨細必陳，由是顧待益厚。

translations.literal: Zhi's nature was loyal and devoted; once he held a post close to the inner court, moved by the sovereign's weighty trust, he wished to repay it in deed, so whenever policy fell short he would report it whether great or small, and for this reason his attentive treatment grew ever deeper.
translations.idiomatic: Devoted by nature, Zhi now served in the emperor's immediate circle. Grateful for Dezong's trust, he sought every way to repay it, and whenever he saw a flaw in policy, large or small, he spoke of it plainly—whereupon the emperor's regard for him only deepened.

sentences.zh: 建中四年，硃泚謀逆，從駕幸奉天。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianzhong, Zhu Ci plotted rebellion, and the emperor followed the court in flight to Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianzhong year 4, Zhu Ci rose in rebellion, and the emperor withdrew with the court to Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 時天下叛亂，機務填委，征發指蹤，千端萬緒，一日之內，詔書數百。

translations.literal: At that time rebellion spread across the realm, administrative duties piled up, levies and deployments were directed in every direction, and matters branched into thousands of threads; within a single day several hundred edicts might issue.
translations.idiomatic: Rebellion had engulfed the empire. Business of state pressed in from every side—levies, troop movements, countless threads of decision—and within one day the court might issue several hundred edicts.

sentences.zh: 贄揮翰起草，思如泉註，初若不經思慮，既成之後，莫不曲盡事情，中於機會；

translations.literal: Zhi wielded the brush to draft them, his thoughts pouring like a spring; at first they seemed to need no deliberation, yet once completed none failed to exhaust the matter and strike the strategic moment;
translations.idiomatic: Zhi drafted these documents, his thoughts flowing like a spring. They seemed to require no forethought, yet every finished text fully addressed the case and hit the moment's need;

sentences.zh: 胥吏簡劄不暇，同舍皆伏其能。

translations.literal: the clerks could not keep pace with the drafts, and his colleagues in the office all acknowledged his ability.
translations.idiomatic: copyists could scarcely keep up with his output, and the other academicians marveled at his gift.

sentences.zh: 轉考功郎中，依前充職。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Ministry of Personnel while continuing his former duties.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Director of the Ministry of Personnel while remaining in his Hanlin post.

sentences.zh: 嘗啟德宗曰：「今盜遍天下，輿駕播遷，陛下宜痛自引過，以感動人心。

translations.literal: He once addressed Dezong, saying, "Now bandits fill the realm and the imperial carriage is driven abroad; Your Majesty should deeply blame yourself to move men's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: He once urged Dezong: "Bandits now overrun the empire and the throne has been driven into exile. Your Majesty should admit fault in earnest and so stir men's hearts.

sentences.zh: 昔成湯以罪己勃興，楚昭以善言復國。

translations.literal: Formerly King Tang blamed himself for his offences and rose anew; King Zhao of Chu through good words recovered his state.
translations.idiomatic: King Tang of old revived his fortunes by confessing guilt; King Zhao of Chu restored his kingdom through frank counsel.

sentences.zh: 陛下誠能不吝改過，以言謝天下，使書詔無忌，臣雖愚陋，可以仰副聖情，庶令反側之徒，革心向化。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty can truly not be sparing in reforming faults and with words apologize to the realm so that proclamations are without reserve, though I be foolish and lowly I can upwardly match the sagely intent, and it may be hoped that the wavering will mend their hearts and turn to allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: "If Your Majesty will truly reform without stint and address the realm in open apology, so that every edict speaks plainly, then even I—though coarse and unworthy—can help match the imperial purpose. Perhaps those who waver will change their hearts and return to loyalty."

sentences.zh: 」德宗然之。

translations.literal: " Dezong agreed.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor accepted this counsel.

sentences.zh: 故奉天所下書詔，雖武夫悍卒，無不揮涕感激，多贄所為也。

translations.literal: Therefore the edicts issued at Fengtian, even rough soldiers and fierce warriors, all waved aside tears in gratitude; most were composed by Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: The proclamations issued at Fengtian—even hardened soldiers—moved men to tears of gratitude; most were Zhi's work.

sentences.zh: 其年冬，議欲以新歲改元。

translations.literal: That winter, the court debated changing the reign title at the new year.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the court considered adopting a new reign title with the coming year.

sentences.zh: 而卜祝之流，皆以國家數鐘百六，凡事宜有變革，以應時數。

translations.literal: Diviners and prayer masters, however, all held that the dynasty's term had reached the cycle of one hundred and six, and that every affair ought to undergo change to respond to the numerical fate of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Soothsayers argued that the dynasty had reached the critical cycle of 106, and that ritual and policy alike should change to answer Heaven's count.

sentences.zh: 上謂贄曰：「往年群臣請上尊號『聖神文武』四字，今緣寇難，諸事並宜改更，眾欲朕舊號之中更加一兩字，其事何如？

translations.literal: The emperor said to Zhi, "In former years the ministers asked that I take the honorific title "Sagely, Divine, Martial, and Cultured"—four characters; now because of the calamity of bandits, all affairs should be altered, and the multitude wish to add one or two more characters within my old title—how does this strike you?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Zhi: "Years ago the ministers urged the epithet "Sagely, Divine, Martial, and Cultured." Now, in these troubles, many want me to add further characters to that title. What do you think?"

sentences.zh: 」贄奏曰：「尊號之興，本非古制。

translations.literal: " Zhi memorialized, saying, "The rise of honorific titles is not an ancient institution.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhi replied: "Honorific titles are not an ancient practice."

sentences.zh: 行於安泰之日，已累謙沖；

translations.literal: Carried out in days of peace and security, they already weary modesty;
translations.idiomatic: Adopted in peaceful times, they already strain humility;

sentences.zh: 襲乎喪亂之時，尤傷事體。

translations.literal: inherited in times of mourning and disorder, they especially harm the proper frame of affairs.
translations.idiomatic: clung to amid disaster and mourning, they wound the polity all the more.

sentences.zh: 今者鑾輿播越，未復宮闈，宗社震驚，尚愆禋祀，中區多梗，大憝猶存。

translations.literal: Now the imperial carriage is driven in exile, the palace not yet restored, the altars shaken in alarm, and the grand sacrifices still neglected; the central regions are much obstructed and the great enemy still stands.
translations.idiomatic: The throne wanders in exile; the palace remains unreclaimed; the state altars tremble and great rites go unperformed; the heartland is choked with enemies and the chief rebel still holds the field.

sentences.zh: 此乃人情向背之秋，天意去就之際，陛下宜深自懲勵，收攬群心，痛自貶損，以謝靈譴，不可近從末議，重益美名。

translations.literal: This is the season when human hearts incline or turn away and Heaven's intent decides to stay or go; Your Majesty should deeply discipline yourself, gather all hearts, bitterly abase yourself, and apologize to divine judgment—you must not draw near the lesser counsel and further increase a glorious name.
translations.idiomatic: This is the hour when hearts choose sides and Heaven weighs whether to stay or depart. Your Majesty should steel yourself, rally every loyalty, humble yourself deeply, and answer Heaven's rebuke—not heed petty counsel that would swell your glorious title.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「卿所奏陳，雖理體甚切，然時運必須小有改跡，亦不可執滯，卿更思量。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "What you have memorialized, though its rationale is very pressing, yet the fortune of the times necessarily requires some small alteration in form, and one cannot be obstinate—think further.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Your reasoning is urgent and sound, yet fate may still demand some outward change. We cannot be rigid—consider further."

sentences.zh: 」贄曰：「古之人君稱號，或稱皇稱帝，或稱王，但一字而已。

translations.literal: " Zhi said, "The titles of rulers of men in antiquity were called emperor or called king, only a single character.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhi said: "Ancient rulers called themselves emperor or king—a single word apiece."

sentences.zh: 至暴秦，乃兼皇帝二字，後代因之。

translations.literal: Only violent Qin united the two characters emperor and sovereign, and later ages followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Only tyrannical Qin joined the two words huang and di, and later dynasties followed suit.

sentences.zh: 及昏僻之君，乃有聖劉、天元之號。

translations.literal: As for benighted and perverse rulers, then there were titles such as Sagely Liu and Heavenly Prime.
translations.idiomatic: Decadent sovereigns invented names like Sagely Liu or Heavenly Prime.

sentences.zh: 是知人主輕重，不在自稱，崇其號無補於徽猷；

translations.literal: From this one knows that the weight of the ruler does not lie in what he calls himself; glorifying his title does not aid his fine government;
translations.idiomatic: A ruler's stature does not rest on what he calls himself. Magnifying his title does not improve his rule;

sentences.zh: 損其名不傷其德美。

translations.literal: diminishing his name does not injure the beauty of his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: trimming his title does not mar his virtue.

sentences.zh: 然而損之有謙光稽古之善，崇之獲矜能納諂之譏，得失不侔，居然可辨。

translations.literal: Yet to diminish it has the good of modest brilliance and antiquity; to glorify it earns the reproach of pride and accepting flattery—the gain and loss are not equal, and plainly may be distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: To shrink it is modest and wise; to enlarge it invites pride and flatters fawning—the one profit, the other loss, is obvious.

sentences.zh: 況今時遭迍否，事屬傾危，尤宜懼思，以自貶抑。

translations.literal: Moreover, the present time meets obstruction and denial and affairs belong to tilting peril; all the more one should fear and reflect, and abase oneself.
translations.idiomatic: In obstruction and peril such as this, fear and self-restraint are all the more needed.

sentences.zh: 必也俯稽術數，須有變更。

translations.literal: If one must bow to numbers and arts of calculation, there must be change.
translations.idiomatic: If omens must be obeyed, then change there must be—

sentences.zh: 與其增美稱而失人心，不若黜舊號以祗天戒。

translations.literal: Rather than augment a glorious title and lose men's hearts, it is better to remove the old title to respect Heaven's warning.
translations.idiomatic: but better to shed the old epithets and honor Heaven's warning than to add glorious words and lose men's hearts.

sentences.zh: 天時人事，理必相符，人既好謙，天亦助順。

translations.literal: Heaven's time and human affairs, principle necessarily correspond; men love modesty, and Heaven also aids the compliant.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and men move together: when men choose humility, Heaven aids the yielding.

sentences.zh: 陛下誠能斷自宸鑒，煥發德音，引咎降名，深示刻責，惟謙與順，一舉而二美從之。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty can decisively judge from the inner mirror and renew a virtuous proclamation, confess guilt and lower your title, deeply display self-reproach—only modesty and compliance, one act and two beauties follow.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty will decide from within, issue a fresh edict, confess fault, shorten his title, and show deep penance—humility and compliance in one stroke win both blessings.

sentences.zh: 」德宗從之，但改興元年號而已。

translations.literal: " Dezong followed this and only changed the reign title to Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong took his advice and changed only the reign name, to Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 初，德宗倉皇出幸，府藏委棄，凝冽之際，士眾多寒，服禦之外，無尺縑丈帛。

translations.literal: At first, when Dezong fled in haste from the capital, treasury stores were abandoned; in the piercing cold, soldiers mostly suffered cold, and apart from clothing none had a foot of silk or an inch of cloth.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong fled the capital in disorder, the treasury was left behind. In biting cold his soldiers shivered, for beyond their uniforms they had neither cloth nor silk.

sentences.zh: 及賊泚解圍，諸籓貢奉繼至，乃於奉天行在貯貢物於廊下，仍題曰「瓊林」、「大盈」二庫名。

translations.literal: When the bandit Zhu Ci's siege was lifted, regional tribute arrived in succession; at the Fengtian traveling palace the tribute goods were stored under the galleries, and still they were labeled with the names of the two treasuries Qionlin and Daying.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhu Ci's siege ended, tribute poured in from the provinces. At the Fengtian encampment these gifts were piled in the corridors under the old palace store labels Qionlin and Daying.

sentences.zh: 贄諫曰：

translations.literal: Zhi remonstrated, saying,
translations.idiomatic: Zhi remonstrated,

sentences.zh: 上嘉納之，令去其題署。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and adopted it, and ordered the labels removed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and had the labels taken down.

sentences.zh: 興元元年，李懷光異志已萌，欲激怒諸軍，上表論諸軍衣糧薄，神策衣糧厚，厚薄不均，難以驅戰，意在撓沮進軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xingyuan, Li Huaiguang's divergent intent had already sprouted; wishing to inflame the armies, he memorialized on the thin clothing and grain of the various armies and the thick clothing and grain of the Shence Army—the unevenness of thick and thin made it difficult to drive them to battle—his intent being to thwart and discourage the advance.
translations.idiomatic: In Xingyuan 1, Li Huaiguang's disloyalty was already evident. To provoke the troops he complained that other armies were underpaid while the Shence units were lavishly supplied, hoping to stall the advance.

sentences.zh: 李晟密奏，恐其有變，上憂之，遣贄使懷光軍宣諭。

translations.literal: Li Sheng secretly memorialized, fearing that Huaiguang might change; the emperor was troubled and sent Zhi to Huaiguang's army to proclaim the imperial will.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sheng warned secretly that Huaiguang might rebel. Uneasy, the emperor dispatched Zhi to announce the throne's intent in Huaiguang's camp.

sentences.zh: 使還，贄奏事曰：

translations.literal: When the envoy returned, Zhi reported on affairs, saying,
translations.idiomatic: On his return Zhi reported,

sentences.zh: 德宗初望懷光回意破賊，故晟屢奏移軍不許；

translations.literal: Dezong at first hoped Huaiguang would turn his heart and destroy the bandits, therefore when Sheng repeatedly memorialized to move the army he did not grant it;
translations.idiomatic: Dezong still hoped Huaiguang would repent and crush the rebels, so he had repeatedly refused Li Sheng's requests to redeploy;

sentences.zh: 及贄縷陳懷光反狀，乃可晟之奏，遂移軍東渭橋。

translations.literal: when Zhi fully set forth Huaiguang's rebellious signs, only then did he grant Sheng's memorial, and the army was moved to East Wei Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: only when Zhi laid out Huaiguang's treason plainly did he allow the move to East Wei Bridge.

sentences.zh: 而鄜坊節度李建徽、神策行營陽惠元猶在咸陽，贄慮懷光並建徽等軍，又奏曰：

translations.literal: Yet Jianwei, military governor of Bin and Fang, and Yang Huiyuan of the Shence field headquarters still remained at Xianyang; Zhi feared Huaiguang would absorb Jianwei and the rest, and again memorialized, saying,
translations.idiomatic: But Li Jianwei of Bin-Fang and Yang Huiyuan of the Shence still camped at Xianyang; fearing Huaiguang might swallow their forces, Zhi memorialized again:

sentences.zh: 德宗曰：「卿之所料極善。

translations.literal: Dezong said, "What you have forecast is excellent.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong said, "Your foresight is excellent.

sentences.zh: 然李晟移軍，懷光心已惆悵，若更遣建徽、惠元就東，則使得為詞。

translations.literal: Yet Li Sheng has moved his army and Huaiguang's heart is already aggrieved; if we further send Jianwei and Huiyuan eastward, we give him grounds for complaint.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Li Sheng has already marched, and Huaiguang's mood is raw. Sending Jianwei and Huiyuan east as well would hand him a grievance.

sentences.zh: 且俟旬時。

translations.literal: Let us wait perhaps ten days.
translations.idiomatic: Wait a fortnight.

sentences.zh: 」晟至東渭橋，不旬日，懷光果奪兩節度兵，建徽單騎遁而獲免，惠元中路被執，害之。

translations.literal: " Within ten days after Sheng reached East Wei Bridge, Huaiguang indeed seized the troops of both commissioners; Jianwei escaped alone on a single horse, while Huiyuan was seized on the road and killed.
translations.idiomatic: " Within ten days Huaiguang seized both armies. Li Jianwei fled alone on horseback; Yang Huiyuan was captured en route and executed.

sentences.zh: 報至行在，人情大恐。

translations.literal: When the report reached the traveling palace, the temper of men was greatly terrified.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, panic spread.

sentences.zh: 翌日，移幸山南。

translations.literal: The next day, the court moved in flight to Shannan.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the emperor withdrew to Shannan.

sentences.zh: 贄練達兵機，率如此類。

translations.literal: Zhi's mastery of military affairs was thorough, and matters of this kind were mostly like this.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi's grasp of military circumstance was as sure as this throughout.

sentences.zh: 二月，從幸梁州，轉諫議大夫，依前充學士。

translations.literal: In the second month he followed in attendance at Liang Prefecture, was transferred to Remonstrating Grand Master, and continued as academician as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month he followed the court to Liangzhou, was made Remonstrating Grand Master, and kept his Hanlin post.

sentences.zh: 先是，鳳翔衙將李楚琳乘涇師之亂，殺節度使張鎰，歸款硃泚。

translations.literal: Previously, the Fengxiang yamen officer Li Chuilin, taking advantage of the disorder of the Jingzhou army, killed Military Governor Zhang Yi and submitted to Zhu Ci.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Li Chuilin, a Fengxiang staff officer, had exploited the Jing army's chaos to murder governor Zhang Yi and submit to Zhu Ci.

sentences.zh: 及奉天解圍，楚琳遣使貢奉，時方艱阻，不獲已，命為鳳翔節度使。

translations.literal: When the Fengtian siege was lifted, Chuilin sent envoys with tribute; the times were dire and the court could not refuse, so he was appointed military governor of Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: After Fengtian was relieved, Chuilin sent tribute. The court, hard pressed, confirmed him as Fengxiang's military governor.

sentences.zh: 然德宗忿其弒逆，心不能容，才至漢中，欲令渾瑊代為節度。

translations.literal: Yet Dezong resented his regicidal crime and in his heart could not bear it; having only reached Hanzhong, he wished to have Hun Zhen replace him as military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong hated his betrayal, and once the court reached Hanzhong he planned to replace him with Hun Zhen.

sentences.zh: 贄諫曰：「楚琳之罪，固不容誅，但以乘輿未復，大憝猶存，勤王之師，悉在畿內，急宣速告，晷刻是爭。

translations.literal: Zhi remonstrated, saying, "Chuilin's crime indeed cannot be pardoned, but because the imperial carriage is not yet restored and the great enemy still stands, the armies that hastened to aid the throne are all within the capital region; urgent proclamation must be swift, and every quarter-hour counts.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi objected: "Chuilin deserves death, but the throne is still in exile and the chief rebel remains. Every loyal army sits in the vicinity, and messages must fly without delay.

sentences.zh: 商嶺則道迂且遙，駱谷復為賊所扼，僅通王命，唯在褒斜，此路若又阻艱，南北便成隔絕。

translations.literal: The Shangling road is circuitous and far, and the Luo Valley is again blocked by bandits; barely the imperial command passes, only through Baoxie—if this road is again obstructed and perilous, north and south will at once be cut off.
translations.idiomatic: The Shangzhou route is long and round; the Luo Valley lies in enemy hands. Only Baoxie still carries the emperor's word—block that pass and north and south are severed.

sentences.zh: 以諸鎮危疑之勢，居二逆誘脅之中，恟々群情，各懷向背。

translations.literal: Among the various commands, in the posture of peril and doubt, between the two rebels' inducement and coercion, the many hearts tumultuously each harbor inclination or turning away.
translations.idiomatic: Every commandery wavers between the two rebels, hearts pulling this way and that.

sentences.zh: 賊勝則往，我勝則來，其間事機，不容差跌。

translations.literal: When the bandits win they go over, when we win they come back; among these the critical junctures cannot suffer a misstep.
translations.idiomatic: They rally to whichever side seems victorious; not a step dare go wrong.

sentences.zh: 儻楚琳發憾，公肆猖狂，南塞要沖，東延巨猾，則我咽喉梗而心膂分矣，其勢豈不病哉！

translations.literal: If Chuilin in resentment vents his rage openly in mad license, blocking the southern chokepoint and extending the great villain eastward, then our throat will be blocked and heart and spine divided—will not the situation be crippling!
translations.idiomatic: Should Chuilin turn vindictive and bar the southern gate while the great foe presses east, our lifeline is cut and our strength split—how crippling that would be!"

sentences.zh: 」上釋然開悟，乃善待楚琳使，優詔安慰其心。

translations.literal: " The emperor, released and enlightened, thereupon treated Chuilin's envoys well and with a generous edict comforted his heart.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor understood and treated Chuilin's envoys with kindness and a reassuring edict.

sentences.zh: 德宗至梁，欲以谷口已北從臣賜號曰「奉天定難功臣」，谷口已南隨扈者曰「元從功臣」，不選朝官，一例俱賜。

translations.literal: When Dezong reached Liang, he wished to bestow on ministers north of the valley mouth the title "Meritorious Ministers Who Settled Calamity in Fengtian," and on those who followed in attendance south of the valley mouth the title "Original Followers as Meritorious Ministers," not selecting among court officials but bestowing alike on all.
translations.idiomatic: At Liangzhou he meant to title everyone north of the valley pass "Ministers Who Quelled Calamity at Fengtian" and everyone south of it "Meritorious Original Followers," granting the honors alike without distinguishing court from camp.

sentences.zh: 贄奏曰：「破賊扞難，武臣之效。

translations.literal: Zhi memorialized, saying, "Destroying bandits and warding off calamity are the achievement of military officers.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi wrote: "Breaking rebels and bearing hardship belong to soldiers.

sentences.zh: 至如宮闈近侍，班列員僚，但馳走從行而已，忽與介胄奮命之士，俱號功臣，伏恐武臣憤惋。

translations.literal: As for those close to the palace and the ranks of officials, they only galloped in attendance—suddenly to rank them with armored men who staked their lives, I fear military officers will be angered and resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendants and civil officers merely rode along—yet they would share the soldiers' title of merit. The army would rage."

sentences.zh: 」乃止。

translations.literal: " Thereupon it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 李晟既收京城，遣中使宣付翰林院具錄先散失宮人名字，令草詔賜渾瑊，遣於奉天尋訪，以得為限，仍量與資糧送赴行在。

translations.literal: When Li Sheng had recovered the capital, he sent palace envoys to instruct the Hanlin Academy to compile a list of palace women scattered in the first flight and draft an edict to give to Hun Zhen, dispatching him to search at Fengtian, taking found persons as the limit, and still measuring out supplies to send them to the traveling court.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Sheng retook Chang'an, he had the Hanlin record palace women lost in the flight and draft an edict for Hun Zhen to find them around Fengtian and send any found to the court with provisions.

sentences.zh: 贄不時奉詔，進狀論之曰：

translations.literal: Zhi did not promptly follow the edict and submitted a statement discussing it, saying,
translations.idiomatic: Zhi did not draft the edict at once and submitted a memorial arguing against it:

sentences.zh: 帝遂不降詔，但遣使而已。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon did not lower the edict, but only sent envoys.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor set the edict aside and sent envoys only.

sentences.zh: 德宗還京，轉中書舍人，學士如故。

translations.literal: When Dezong returned to the capital, Zhi was transferred to Drafting Attendant of the Secretariat while remaining academician as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong returned to Chang'an, Zhi became Drafting Attendant of the Secretariat while retaining his Hanlin post.

sentences.zh: 初，贄受張鎰知，得居內職；

translations.literal: At first, Zhi received Zhang Yi's recognition and obtained an inner-court post;
translations.idiomatic: Zhi owed his inner-court post to Zhang Yi's patronage;

sentences.zh: 及鎰為盧杞所排，贄常憂惴；

translations.literal: when Yi was displaced by Lu Qi, Zhi was constantly anxious;
translations.idiomatic: when Qi drove Yi out, Zhi lived in fear;

sentences.zh: 及杞貶黜，始敢上書言事。

translations.literal: only when Qi was demoted and dismissed did he dare to submit memorials on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: only after Qi's fall did he dare speak freely in memorials.

sentences.zh: 德宗好文，益深顧遇。

translations.literal: Dezong loved literature and his deep attentive regard grew.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong admired fine writing and favored him all the more.

sentences.zh: 奉天解圍後，德宗言及違離宗廟，嗚咽流涕曰：「致寇之由，實朕之過。

translations.literal: After Fengtian's siege was lifted, when Dezong spoke of departing from the ancestral temples, he sobbed with flowing tears, saying, "The cause that brought bandits was truly my fault.
translations.idiomatic: After Fengtian was saved, Dezong wept at having left the ancestral shrines, saying, "The bandits are my own doing.

sentences.zh: 」贄亦流涕而對曰：「臣思致今日之患者，群臣之罪也。

translations.literal: " Zhi also wept in reply, saying, "Your servant thinks that those who brought about today's calamity are the crime of the ministers.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhi wept in answer: "The ministers brought today's disaster upon Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 」贄意蓋為盧杞、趙贊等也。

translations.literal: " Zhi's intent covered Lu Qi, Zhao Zan, and others.
translations.idiomatic: He meant Lu Qi, Zhao Zan, and their like.

sentences.zh: 上欲掩杞之失，則曰：「雖朕德薄，致茲禍亂，亦運數前定，事不由人。

translations.literal: The emperor wishing to cover Qi's faults, then said, "Though my virtue is thin and brought this calamity and disorder, it is also the prior determination of numerical fate, and the affair was not in men's hands.
translations.idiomatic: Wishing to shield Qi, the emperor said, "My virtue is thin and invited this chaos—but fate had already decreed it; men could not avert it.

sentences.zh: 」贄又極言杞等罪狀，上雖貌從，心頗不說。

translations.literal: " Zhi again fully set forth Qi and others' crimes; the emperor outwardly acquiesced but inwardly was quite displeased.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhi again denounced Qi at length. Dezong assented in appearance but took offense.

sentences.zh: 吳通微兄弟俱在翰林，亦承德宗寵遇，文章才器不迨贄；

translations.literal: The brothers Wu Tongwei were all in the Hanlin and also received Dezong's favor; their literary talent and capacity did not reach Zhi;
translations.idiomatic: The brothers Wu Tongwei served in the Hanlin and shared the emperor's favor, though their literary gifts fell short of Zhi's;

sentences.zh: 而能交結權幸，共短贄於上前。

translations.literal: yet they could form ties with powerful favorites and together slander Zhi before the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: yet they courted the powerful and slandered Zhi before the throne.

sentences.zh: 故劉從一、姜公輔自卑品蒼黃之中，皆登輔相；

translations.literal: Therefore Liu Congyi and Jiang Gongfu from low rank in the yellow confusion all ascended to chief ministers;
translations.idiomatic: Thus Liu Congyi and Jiang Gongfu rose from obscurity straight to the highest offices;

sentences.zh: 而贄為朋黨所擠，同職害其能，加以言事激切，動失上之歡心，故久之不為輔相。

translations.literal: whereas Zhi was squeezed out by faction, colleagues harmed by his ability, and moreover his remonstrances were sharp and he repeatedly lost the sovereign's pleasure, and so for a long time he was not made chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: while Zhi, squeezed by factions and envied by peers, and further estranging the emperor with blunt counsel, long went without the premiership.

sentences.zh: 其於議論應對，明練理體，敷陳剖判，下筆如神，當時名流，無不推挹。

translations.literal: In discussion and response, he was clear and practiced in principle, in exposition and judgment he wrote as if inspired; the celebrated men of the time all without exception esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: In debate and reply he was lucid and principled; in memorials his pen seemed inspired; contemporaries unanimously revered him.

sentences.zh: 貞元初，李抱真入朝，從容奏曰：「陛下幸奉天、山南時，赦書至山東，宣諭之時，士卒無不感泣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenyuan, when Li Baozhen entered court, he calmly memorialized, saying, "When Your Majesty was at Fengtian and Shannan, the amnesty when proclaimed in Shandong, at the time of proclamation, soldiers without exception wept.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenyuan, Li Baozhen came to court and said calmly: "When Your Majesty was at Fengtian and Shannan, the amnesty reaching Shandong moved every soldier to tears at its reading.

sentences.zh: 臣即時見人情如此，知賊不足平也。

translations.literal: Your servant at that time saw human hearts thus and knew the bandits could not long stand.
translations.idiomatic: "I saw men's hearts then and knew the rebels could not endure."

sentences.zh: 時贄母韋氏在江東，上遣中使迎至京師，搢紳榮之。

translations.literal: At that time Zhi's mother the Lady Wei was in Jiangdong; the emperor sent palace envoys to escort her to the capital, and the gentry counted it an honor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi's mother Lady Wei was still in the lower Yangtze; the emperor sent eunuchs to bring her to the capital, to the envy of the court.

sentences.zh: 俄丁母憂，東歸洛陽，寓居嵩山豐樂寺。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he entered mourning for his mother, returned east to Luoyang, and lodged at Fengle Temple on Mount Song.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he began mourning for her, went east to Luoyang, and lived at Fengle Temple on Mount Song.

sentences.zh: 籓鎮賻贈及別陳餉遺，一無所取。

translations.literal: Condolence gifts from military governors and separate private offerings, he took none.
translations.idiomatic: He accepted no condolence gifts from the provinces nor any private offerings.

sentences.zh: 與韋臯布衣時相善，唯西川致遺，奏而受之。

translations.literal: With Wei Gao he had been friendly as commoners; only from Xichuan came gifts, which he reported and accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Only Wei Gao of Xichuan, an old friend from commoner days, might send gifts—and then only after Zhi reported them and was told to accept.

sentences.zh: 贄父初葬蘇州，至是欲合葬。

translations.literal: Zhi's father's burial at first was in Suzhou; now he wished to conduct a joint burial.
translations.idiomatic: His father had been buried first in Suzhou; he now wished to reinter him beside his mother.

sentences.zh: 上遣中使護其柩車至洛，其禮遇如此。

translations.literal: The emperor sent palace envoys to escort the coffin carriage to Luoyang; his treatment was thus.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent eunuchs to escort the coffin to Luoyang—such was the honor shown him.

sentences.zh: 免喪，權知兵部侍郎，依前充學士。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he was appointed acting Vice Minister of War while continuing as academician.
translations.idiomatic: After his mourning period he served as acting Vice Minister of War and retained his Hanlin post.

sentences.zh: 申謝日，贄伏地而泣，德宗為之改容敘慰。

translations.literal: On the day he presented thanks, Zhi prostrated himself and wept; Dezong for this changed his expression and consoled him.
translations.idiomatic: When he came to offer thanks, Zhi fell prostrate and wept; the emperor softened his face and comforted him.

sentences.zh: 恩遇既隆，中外屬意為輔弼，而宰相竇參素忌贄，贄亦短參之所為，言參黷貨，由是與參不平。

translations.literal: His gracious treatment was already lofty, and within and without the court looked to him as chief minister; yet Chief Minister Dou Can had long resented Zhi, and Zhi also criticized Can's conduct, saying Can was corrupt in goods, and for this reason he was at odds with Can.
translations.idiomatic: Favor ran high and the court expected him for the premiership, but Dou Can had long envied him; Zhi in turn denounced Can's corruption, and the two were estranged.

sentences.zh: 七年，罷學士，正拜兵部侍郎，知貢舉。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was removed as academician, formally appointed Vice Minister of War, and put in charge of the civil service examinations.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 he left the Hanlin, was confirmed as Vice Minister of War, and supervised the metropolitan examinations.

sentences.zh: 時崔元翰、梁肅文藝冠時，贄輸心於肅。

translations.literal: At that time Cui Yuanhan and Liang Su topped the age in literary art; Zhi gave his heart to Su.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yuanhan and Liang Su then led the literary world; Zhi aligned himself closely with Liang Su.

sentences.zh: 肅與元翰推薦藝實之士，升第之日，雖眾望不愜，然一歲選士，才十四五，數年之內，居臺省清近者十余人。

translations.literal: Su together with Yuanhan recommended men of genuine talent; on the day degrees were awarded, though public expectation was not satisfied, yet in one year's selection of scholars there were only fourteen or fifteen, and within several years more than ten held posts in the Censorate and Secretariat that were clear and near.
translations.idiomatic: Su and Yuanhan advanced men of real ability. Public opinion grumbled at one year's thin harvest—only fourteen or fifteen passed—but within a few years more than ten of them sat in the Censorate and the inner secretariat.

sentences.zh: 八年四月，竇參得罪，以贄為中書侍郎、門下同平章事。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the eighth year Dou Can was guilty of an offence and Zhi was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Chief Minister with the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of year 8, when Dou Can fell, Zhi was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Chief Minister.

sentences.zh: 贄久為邪黨所擠，困而得位，意在不負恩獎，悉心報國，以天下事為己任。

translations.literal: Zhi had long been squeezed out by the wicked faction; gaining office in hardship, his intent was not to fail the grace and reward, to devote his heart to serving the state, and to take the realm's affairs as his own charge.
translations.idiomatic: Long shut out by hostile factions, he at last reached office in adversity, resolved to repay the throne's trust, serve the state with all his heart, and shoulder the empire's business as his own.

sentences.zh: 上即位之初，用楊炎、盧杞秉政，樹立朋黨，排擯良善，卒致天下沸騰，鑾輿奔播。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the emperor's accession he employed Yang Yan and Lu Qi to hold power, established partisan cliques, and excluded the good, until at last the realm seethed and the imperial carriage was driven in flight.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Dezong's reign Yang Yan and Lu Qi held power, built factions, and drove out the worthy until the empire boiled over and the court fled.

sentences.zh: 懲是之失，貞元已後，雖立輔臣，至於小官除擬，上必再三詳問，久之方下。

translations.literal: Chastened by these failures, after Zhenyuan, though chief ministers were appointed, even for minor offices and appointments the emperor would inquire in detail again and again, and only after a long time would he issue the order.
translations.idiomatic: Learning from that disaster, after Zhenyuan he still named chief ministers—but even petty appointments were questioned again and again before an order went out.

sentences.zh: 及贄知政事，請許臺省長官自薦屬官，仍保任之，事有曠敗，兼坐舉主。

translations.literal: When Zhi took part in government, he asked that heads of the Censorate and Secretariat offices be permitted to recommend their subordinate officials and still guarantee them; if affairs were neglected or failed, the recommender would share guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Once in power Zhi proposed that bureau chiefs recommend their own subordinates under guarantee: if a nominee failed in office, the recommender would share the blame.

sentences.zh: 上許之，俄又宣旨曰：「外議云：『諸司所舉，多引用親黨，兼通賂遺，不得實才。

translations.literal: The emperor granted this, but shortly afterward again proclaimed, "Outside opinion says: 'What the various offices recommend mostly draws on kin and partisans, and also passes bribes and gifts, so that real talent is not obtained.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed, then soon announced: "Critics say bureau recommendations favor kin and cronies and trade in bribes, so true talent is lost.

sentences.zh: 』此法行之非便，今後卿等宜自選擇，勿用諸司延薦。

translations.literal: ' This law in operation is not convenient; hereafter you ministers should choose for yourselves and not use the various offices' extended recommendations.
translations.idiomatic: " This method will not do. Hereafter choose your own men—do not rely on bureau referrals.

sentences.zh: 」贄論奏曰：

translations.literal: " Zhi memorialized in discussion, saying,
translations.idiomatic: " Zhi argued in a memorial:

sentences.zh: 上雖嘉其所陳，長官薦士之詔，竟追寢之。

translations.literal: The emperor though he praised what he set forth, the edict on bureau chiefs recommending scholars was in the end pursued and suspended.
translations.idiomatic: Though the emperor praised his reasoning, the recommendation edict was withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 國朝舊制，吏部選人，每年調集。

translations.literal: The dynasty's old system: the Ministry of Personnel selected candidates and gathered them each year.
translations.idiomatic: Under former usage the Ministry of Personnel convened candidates annually.

sentences.zh: 自乾元已後，屬宿兵於野。

translations.literal: From after Qianyuan, because troops were quartered in the field,
translations.idiomatic: After Qianyuan, with armies camped in the field,

sentences.zh: 歲或兇荒，遂三年一置選。

translations.literal: when the year sometimes had famine and disaster, selection was then held once every three years.
translations.idiomatic: famine years led to holding the selection only once every three years.

sentences.zh: 由是選人停擁，其數猥多，文書不接，真偽難辨，吏緣為奸，註授乖濫，而有十年不得調者。

translations.literal: From this candidates piled up in suspension, their numbers grossly many, documents did not connect, truth and falsehood were hard to distinguish, clerks used this to practice fraud, registration and appointment were confused and excessive, and there were those ten years without transfer.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates then backed up in vast numbers; records failed to match; clerks grew corrupt; appointments went awry; some men waited ten years without a posting.

sentences.zh: 贄奏吏部分內外官員為三分，計闕集人，每年置選。

translations.literal: Zhi memorialized that the Ministry of Personnel divide inner and outer officials into three parts, calculate vacancies and gather men, and hold selection each year.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi had the ministry divide civil posts into three tiers, tally vacancies, and restore annual selection.

sentences.zh: 故選司之弊，十去七八，天下稱之。

translations.literal: Therefore the abuses of the selection office were seven or eight tenths removed, and the realm praised it.
translations.idiomatic: Seven or eight tenths of the selection office's abuses vanished, and the empire applauded.

sentences.zh: 贄與賈耽、盧邁、趙憬同知政事，百司有所申覆，皆更讓不言可否。

translations.literal: Zhi together with Jia Dan, Lu Mai, and Zhao Jing jointly handled government affairs; when the hundred offices had matters to report for review, all would defer in turn and not speak whether they approved or not.
translations.idiomatic: Serving with Jia Dan, Lu Mai, and Zhao Jing, Zhi joined in governing; when ministries submitted business for review, each minister deferred to the next and none would say yea or nay.

sentences.zh: 舊例，宰臣當旬，秉筆決事，每十日一易，贄請準故事，令秉筆者以應之。

translations.literal: By old precedent, chief ministers in rotation on the ten-day cycle held the brush and decided affairs, changing every ten days; Zhi asked to follow precedent and have the one holding the brush respond.
translations.idiomatic: By custom the chief minister on duty held the brush and decided cases, rotating every ten days; Zhi asked to restore that practice.

sentences.zh: 又以河隴陷蕃已來，西北邊常以重兵守備，謂之防秋，皆河南、江淮諸鎮之軍也，更番往來，疲於戍役。

translations.literal: Moreover, since the He and Long regions fell to the Tibetans, the northwest border constantly used heavy troops for defense, called autumn defense; all were armies of the commands south of the Yellow River and of the Jiang and Huai, rotating in turn, weary from garrison duty.
translations.idiomatic: Since Hexi and Longyou fell to Tibet, the northwest relied on "autumn defense"—troops rotated from the Huai and the Yellow River south, worn out by endless garrison tours.

sentences.zh: 贄以中原之兵，不習邊事，及扞虜戰賊，多有敗衄，又苦邊將名目太多，諸軍統制不一，緩急無以應敵，乃上疏論其事曰：

translations.literal: Zhi held that the armies of the central plains did not practice border affairs, and in resisting barbarians and fighting bandits many suffered defeat; he also grieved that border generals' titles were too many and the various armies' unified control was not one, so in urgency and ease there was no means to meet the enemy—thereupon he submitted a memorial discussing the matter, saying,
translations.idiomatic: Central armies, unused to frontier war, often broke against barbarians and rebels; too many frontier commanders divided control; in crisis no one could respond—so Zhi memorialized at length:

sentences.zh: 德宗極深嘉納，優詔褒獎之。

translations.literal: Dezong extremely and deeply praised and adopted it, and with a generous edict rewarded and commended him.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong warmly approved and issued a commendatory edict.

sentences.zh: 贄在中書，政不便於時者，多所條奏。

translations.literal: When Zhi was in the Secretariat, where government was not convenient to the times, he many times submitted items in memorial.
translations.idiomatic: In the Secretariat Zhi repeatedly memorialized on policies that ill suited the age.

sentences.zh: 德宗雖不能皆可，而心頗重之。

translations.literal: Dezong though he could not approve all, yet in his heart greatly valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong could not accept every proposal, yet valued him deeply.

sentences.zh: 初，竇參既貶郴州，節度使劉士寧餉參絹數千匹。

translations.literal: At first, after Dou Can was demoted to Chen Prefecture, Military Governor Liu Shining presented Can several thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: After Dou Can was banished to Chenzhou, Liu Shining, his military governor, sent him thousands of bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 湖南觀察使李巽與參有隙，具事奏聞，德宗不悅。

translations.literal: Hunan Observation Commissioner Li Xun had a rift with Can and reported the whole affair; Dezong was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xun of Hunan, Can's enemy, reported the gift; Dezong took offense.

sentences.zh: 會右庶子姜公輔於上前聞奏，稱「竇參嘗語臣云：陛下怒臣未已」，德宗怒，再貶參，竟殺之。

translations.literal: It happened that Right Assistant to the Heir Apparent Jiang Gongfu heard and reported before the sovereign, saying, "Dou Can once told your servant: the Emperor's anger at your servant is not yet ended," and Dezong was angry, demoted Can again, and in the end killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Gongfu then told the throne that Can had said, "The Emperor's wrath against me is not spent." Dezong raged, demoted Can again, and finally had him executed.

sentences.zh: 時議雲公輔奏竇參語得之於贄，雲參之死，贄有力焉。

translations.literal: Contemporary opinion said Gongfu's report of Can's words was obtained from Zhi, and that in Can's death Zhi had force.
translations.idiomatic: Gossip held that Jiang Gongfu's testimony came from Zhi and that Zhi had helped bring about Can's death.

sentences.zh: 又素惡於公異、於邵，既輔政而逐之，談者亦以為厄。

translations.literal: He had also long been at odds with Gongyi and Yu Shao; once he aided government he drove them out, and talkers also regarded this as ill omen.
translations.idiomatic: He had long feuded with Gongyi and Yu Shao; once in power he expelled them—another mark against him in rumor.

sentences.zh: 戶部侍郎、判度支裴延齡，奸宄用事，天下嫉之如仇。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Revenue and Acting Commissioner of Revenue Pei Yanling, a wicked villain wielding power, the realm hated him as an enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yanling, Vice Minister of Revenue and fiscal commissioner, was a corrupt manipulator whom the empire hated like a foe.

sentences.zh: 以得幸於天子，無敢言者。

translations.literal: Because he won the Son of Heaven's favor, none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: Favored by the emperor, he went largely unchallenged.

sentences.zh: 贄獨以身當之，屢於延英面陳其不可，累上疏極言其弊。

translations.literal: Zhi alone with his person confronted him, repeatedly in Yanying Hall face to face stating that he could not be allowed, and many times submitted memorials fully stating his abuses.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi alone stood against him, arguing repeatedly in Yanying Hall and flooding the throne with memorials on his abuses.

sentences.zh: 延齡日加譖毀。

translations.literal: Yanling daily increased slander and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Yanling daily slandered him the more.

sentences.zh: 十年十二月，除太子賓客，罷知政事。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the tenth year he was appointed Crown Prince Guest and ceased handling government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of year 10 he was made Crown Prince Guest and removed from government.

sentences.zh: 贄性畏慎，及策免私居，朝謁之外，不通賓客，無所過從。

translations.literal: Zhi's nature was fearful and cautious; once dismissed by edict and living privately, apart from court audience he did not receive guests and had no associations.
translations.idiomatic: Cautious by nature, after his dismissal he saw no one beyond required audiences.

sentences.zh: 十一年春，旱，邊軍芻粟不給，具事論訴；

translations.literal: In the spring of the eleventh year there was drought; frontier armies' fodder and grain were not supplied, and they fully stated the matter in complaint and appeal;
translations.idiomatic: In spring of year 11 drought struck; frontier troops lacked fodder and grain and petitioned in distress;

sentences.zh: 延齡言贄與張滂、李充等搖動軍情，語在《延齡傳》。

translations.literal: Yanling said Zhi together with Zhang Pang and Li Chong and others were shaking army morale—the words are in the "Biography of Yanling."
translations.idiomatic: Yanling accused Zhi, Zhang Pang, and Li Chong of stirring the armies—the account is in Yanling's biography.

sentences.zh: 德宗怒，將誅贄等四人，會諫議大夫陽城等極言論奏，乃貶贄為忠州別駕。

translations.literal: Dezong was angry and was about to execute Zhi and the other four men; it happened that Remonstrating Grand Master Yang Cheng and others fully argued in memorial, and thereupon Zhi was demoted to Assistant Administrator of Zhong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong would have executed Zhi and three others, but Yang Cheng and other remonstrators protested fiercely; Zhi was banished instead as assistant administrator of Zhongzhou.

sentences.zh: 贄初入翰林，特承德宗異顧，歌詩戲狎，朝夕陪遊。

translations.literal: When Zhi first entered the Hanlin, he especially received Dezong's unusual regard, singing poems and playful intimacy, morning and evening accompanying in travel.
translations.idiomatic: Entering the Hanlin, Zhi enjoyed Dezong's special favor—verses, banter, constant companionship.

sentences.zh: 及出居艱阻之中，雖有宰臣，而謀猷參決，多出於贄，故當時目為「內相」。

translations.literal: When he went out and dwelt amid hardship and peril, though there were chief ministers, yet planning and counsel for joint decision mostly came from Zhi, and therefore at the time he was styled the "inner chief minister."
translations.idiomatic: In the flight from Chang'an, though titular chief ministers remained, strategy flowed from Zhi; men called him the "inner prime minister."

sentences.zh: 從幸山南，道途艱險，扈從不及，與帝相失，一夕不至，上喻軍士曰：「得贄者賞千金。

translations.literal: Following in attendance at Shannan, the road was perilous and hard; the escort could not keep up, and he lost the emperor; one night he did not arrive, and the emperor told the soldiers, "Whoever gets Zhi will be rewarded a thousand in gold.
translations.idiomatic: On the road to Shannan he fell behind the escort and missed the emperor for a night; Dezong told the troops, "A thousand in gold to whoever finds Zhi.

sentences.zh: 」翌日贄謁見，上喜形顏色，其寵待如此。

translations.literal: " The next day Zhi paid his respects and was received; the emperor's joy showed in his face—such was his favor and treatment.
translations.idiomatic: " The next day Zhi appeared; the emperor's delight showed on his face—such was his standing.

sentences.zh: 既與二吳不協，漸加浸潤，恩禮稍薄；

translations.literal: Once he was not in harmony with the two Wus, gradual soaking slander was added, and gracious rites grew somewhat thin;
translations.idiomatic: After he fell out with the Wu brothers, slander seeped in and imperial warmth cooled;

sentences.zh: 及通玄敗，上知誣枉，遂復見用。

translations.literal: when Tongxuan was defeated, the emperor knew the false charge and injustice, and thereupon he was again employed.
translations.idiomatic: when Wu Tongxuan fell, the emperor saw the injustice and restored him.

sentences.zh: 贄以受人主殊遇，不敢愛身，事有不可，極言無隱。

translations.literal: Zhi because he received the ruler's special treatment dared not spare his person; where affairs could not be, he spoke to the limit without concealment.
translations.idiomatic: Honored by the throne, he would not spare himself; where policy erred he spoke without reserve.

sentences.zh: 朋友規之，以為太峻，贄曰：「吾上不負天子，下不負吾所學，不恤其他。

translations.literal: Friends admonished him, thinking him too severe; Zhi said, "I above do not fail the Son of Heaven, below do not fail what I have studied—I do not care for the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Friends warned him he was too harsh; Zhi said, "I owe the emperor my loyalty and my learning my integrity—that is enough.

sentences.zh: 」精於吏事，斟酌決斷，不失錙銖。

translations.literal: " He was expert in administrative affairs, weighing and deciding without losing a speck or grain.
translations.idiomatic: " He mastered administration, weighing every decision to the last grain.

sentences.zh: 嘗以「詞詔所出，中書舍人之職，軍興之際，促迫應務，權令學士代之；

translations.literal: He once said, "Proclamations issued belong to the drafting attendant of the Secretariat's office; in times of military rise, pressed and urgent in answering tasks, it was temporarily ordered that academicians replace them;
translations.idiomatic: He argued that edicts belonged to the Secretariat drafters; in wartime Hanlin scholars had substituted only as an emergency measure;

sentences.zh: 朝野乂寧，合歸職分，其命將相制詔，卻付中書行譴。

translations.literal: when court and realm are at peace, they should return to their proper duties; orders to generals and chancellors for edicts should be handed back to the Secretariat to issue.
translations.idiomatic: in peace they should return to their posts, and appointments of generals and ministers should go through the Secretariat again.

sentences.zh: 」又言「學士私臣，玄宗初令待詔，止於唱和文章而已」。

translations.literal: " He also said, "Academicians are private ministers; Xuanzong at first ordered them to await summons, only for harmonizing in literary pieces."
translations.idiomatic: " Hanlin scholars were private retainers; Xuanzong first meant them only for literary companionship."

sentences.zh: 物議是之。

translations.literal: Public opinion approved this.
translations.idiomatic: Opinion sided with him.

sentences.zh: 德宗以贄指斥通微、通玄，故不可其奏。

translations.literal: Dezong because Zhi pointed and reproached Tongwei and Tongxuan, therefore did not approve his memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong rejected the proposal because it targeted the Wu brothers.

sentences.zh: 贄在忠州十年，常閉關靜處，人不識其面，復避謗，不著書。

translations.literal: Zhi at Zhong Prefecture for ten years constantly shut his gates and dwelt in quiet; men did not know his face; he also avoided slander and did not write books.
translations.idiomatic: For ten years at Zhongzhou he lived behind closed gates, unknown by sight, shunning controversy and publishing nothing.

sentences.zh: 家居瘴鄉，人多癘疫，乃抄撮方書，為《陸氏集驗方》五十卷，行於代。

translations.literal: His home was in a miasma region where many suffered plague; he thereupon copied and extracted formulary books and made fifty scrolls of the "Lu Clan Collected Verified Prescriptions," circulating in the generation.
translations.idiomatic: In that malarial country he compiled fifty scrolls of the Lu Clan Collected Verified Prescriptions, which circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 初，贄秉政，貶駕部員外郎李吉甫為明州長史，量移忠州刺史。

translations.literal: At first, when Zhi held government, he demoted Vice Director of the Imperial Transport Li Jifu to Long Administrator of Ming Prefecture, and by measured transfer moved him to Prefect of Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: While in power he had demoted Li Jifu to a distant post, later shifting him to prefect of Zhongzhou.

sentences.zh: 贄在忠州，與吉甫相遇，昆弟、門人鹹為贄憂，而吉甫忻然厚禮，都不銜前事，以宰相禮事之，猶恐其未信不安，日與贄相狎，若平生交契者。

translations.literal: Zhi at Zhong Prefecture met Jifu; brothers and disciples all were anxious for Zhi, yet Jifu gladly and with thick courtesy, entirely not harboring former matters, with chief minister's rites served him, still fearing he had not believed and was uneasy, daily intimate with Zhi as if a lifelong bond.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhongzhou Zhi met Jifu; friends feared revenge, but Jifu received him with lavish courtesy, never mentioning the past, treating him like a chief minister and daily seeking his company as of old.

sentences.zh: 贄初猶慚懼，後乃深交。

translations.literal: Zhi at first was still ashamed and fearful, but afterward they became deep friends.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was wary at first, then came to trust him deeply.

sentences.zh: 時論以吉甫為長者。

translations.literal: Contemporary opinion regarded Jifu as a man of magnanimity.
translations.idiomatic: Men praised Jifu as magnanimous.

sentences.zh: 後有薛延者，代吉甫為刺史，延朝辭日，德宗令宣旨慰安。

translations.literal: Later there was Xue Yan, who replaced Jifu as prefect; on the day Yan took court leave, Dezong ordered the proclamation of an edict to comfort and reassure.
translations.idiomatic: When Xue Yan succeeded Jifu as prefect, Dezong sent a comforting edict on his departure.

sentences.zh: 而韋臯累上表請以贄代己。

translations.literal: Yet Wei Gao repeatedly submitted memorials asking to have Zhi replace himself.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Gao of Xichuan repeatedly asked the throne to recall Zhi in his stead.

sentences.zh: 順宗即位，與陽城、鄭余慶同詔征還。

translations.literal: When Shunzong ascended, together with Yang Cheng and Zheng Yuqing he was summoned back by the same edict.
translations.idiomatic: Shunzong's accession brought edicts recalling Zhi with Yang Cheng and Zheng Yuqing.

sentences.zh: 詔未至而贄卒，時年五十二，贈兵部尚書，謚曰宣。

translations.literal: The edict had not arrived when Zhi died, aged fifty-two; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of War, posthumous name Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Before the summons reached him Zhi died at fifty-two, posthumously honored as Minister of War with the posthumous name Xuan.

sentences.zh: 子簡禮，登進士第，累辟使府。

translations.literal: His son Jianli passed the jinshi and was repeatedly summoned to commissioner staffs.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lu Jianli took the jinshi and served repeatedly in provincial staffs.

sentences.zh: 【史評】史臣曰：近代論陸宣公，比漢之賈誼，而高邁之行，剛正之節，經國成務之要，激切仗義之心，初蒙天子重知，末塗淪躓，皆相類也。

translations.literal: [Historian's appraisal] The historiographer says: In recent times those who discuss Lord Xuan of Lu compare him to Jia Yi of Han, while in lofty conduct, upright integrity, the essentials of ordering the state, and a heart of urgent righteousness—at first receiving the Son of Heaven's weighty knowledge, in the last course falling into ruin—all are alike.
translations.idiomatic: [Historian's appraisal] The annalist writes: Later ages compare Lord Xuan of Lu to Han's Jia Yi—alike in noble bearing, upright spine, statecraft, and fierce loyalty, alike in early favor and final ruin.

sentences.zh: 而誼止中大夫，贄及臺鉉，不為不遇矣。

translations.literal: Yet Yi stopped at Grand Master of the Palace, while Zhi reached the terrace and chief minister's seat—not failing to be favored.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yi rose only to Grand Master of the Palace while Zhi reached the highest office—hardly ill treated.

sentences.zh: 昔公孫鞅挾三策說秦王，淳于髡以隱語見齊君，從古以還，正言不易。

translations.literal: Formerly Gongsun Yang carried three policies to persuade King Zhaoxiang of Qin, and Chunyu Kun with hidden words appeared before the ruler of Qi—from antiquity until now, straight words are not easy.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Yang pleaded three reforms to Qin; Chunyu Kun spoke in riddles to Qi—from antiquity frank counsel has been hard.

sentences.zh: 昔周昭戒急論議，正為此也。

translations.literal: Formerly King Zhao of Zhou warned against hasty discussion—just for this reason.
translations.idiomatic: King Zhao of Zhou warned against rash speech for the same reason.

sentences.zh: 贄居珥筆之列，調飪之地，欲以片心除眾弊，獨手遏群邪，君上不亮其誠，群小共攻其短，欲無放逐，其可得乎！

translations.literal: Zhi dwelt in the ranks of those who tucked the brush behind the ear, in the place of seasoning broth, wishing with a single heart to remove the multitude of abuses, with one hand to block the crowd of wickedness; the ruler above did not illumine his sincerity, the petty together attacked his shortcomings—wishing not to be exiled, how could it be obtained!
translations.idiomatic: Zhi sat where edicts were drafted, wanting one loyal heart to cure a hundred ills and one hand to hold back a host of villains; the throne did not see his sincerity, petty men assailed his faults—exile was inevitable.

sentences.zh: 《詩》稱「其維哲人，告之話言」，又有「誨爾」、「聽我」之恨，此皆賢人君子，嘆言不見用也。

translations.literal: The Odes says, "There is the wise man—tell him frank words," and again has the regret of "I teach you" and "hearken to me"—these are all worthy men and gentlemen lamenting that words are not employed.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Odes praises the wise man who hears plain speech and mourns those who refuse "I teach you" and "hearken to me"—the sigh of sages unused.

sentences.zh: 故堯咨禹拜，千載一時，攜手提耳，豈容易哉！

translations.literal: Therefore Yao consulted and Yu bowed—a thousand years' one moment; taking hand and lifting ear—is it easily done!
translations.idiomatic: When Yao questioned and Yu bowed, the age saw such trust once; to lead by the hand and speak at the ear is no easy thing.

sentences.zh: 【贊】贊曰：良臣悟主，我有嘉猷。

translations.literal: [Appraisal] The appraisal says: A good minister awakens his lord; I have fine plans.
translations.idiomatic: [Appraisal] Appraisal: The worthy minister enlightens his ruler; I offer good counsel.

sentences.zh: 多僻之君，為善不周。

translations.literal: A ruler of many crooked ways does not complete the good.
translations.idiomatic: A perverse sovereign does not finish what is right.

sentences.zh: 忠言救失，啟沃曰讎。

translations.literal: Loyal words remedy failure; earnest counsel is called an enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal speech repairs error; frank admonition is named hostility.

sentences.zh: 勿貽天問，蒼昊悠悠。

translations.literal: Do not bequeath Heaven a question—blue Heaven is vast and far.
translations.idiomatic: Do not leave Heaven unanswered—azure Heaven stretches endless and remote.
